text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Bulgaria's President Petar Stoyanov met exiled king Simeon II and said he would be willing to hold a referendum on restoring the monarchy if parliament voted for it.

-- Bulgaria's anti-communist Union of Democratic Forces (UDF), favoured to win Saturday's general election, is expected to urge early local council elections once the new parliament is formed, a UDF official said.
-- The United States are expected to extend some $7 million to Bulgaria for buying medicines and foods, Bulgaria's Social care minister Ivan Neikov said.

-- Bulgaria hopes to receive some $40 million for the construction of the Sofia underground railway under a possible restructuring of part of former Soviet Union debt to Bulgaria, Prime minister Stefan Sofianski said upon return from Moscow. Russia took over some $100 million of Soviet Union debt to Bulgaria after the USSR disintegrated.

-- Bulgaria was expected to choose a buyer of a 51 percent stake in the state owned cement producer Zlatna Panega by May 10 and the sale was expected to be finalised after the new parliament approved a concession on the nearby lime quarry, the Construction ministry said.
-- Bulgaria's state owned Expressbank posted some 1.4 billion levs net profit for last year, the bank's balance sheet showed.
-- Bulgaria's biggest oil refinery Neftochim owes some 200 billion levs to the budget in customs and excise duty arrears, Neftochim's financial director Atanas Zaikov said.

-- Ten foreign banks have applied for advisers to the Privatisation Agency (PA) on the sale of major Bulgarian state plants, PA executive director Alexander Sabotinov said. The Agency announced last month it was seeking financial advisers for the privatisation of 22 large state companies.

-- Foreign investors have invested some $100 million in Bulgarian domestic bad debt bonds between the beginning of March and April 11, eyeing pending sell-offs, a central bank official said. The bonds are accepted as means of payment in privatisation at par value.
-- The British Rover group is interested in assembling Rover military jeeps in Bulgaria, the British ambassador in Sofia Roger Short said.
-- Bulgaria's domestic debt fell by 294 billion levs in March to 2.484 trillion levs due to the lev rise against the dollar, Finance ministry figures showed.
-- The Russian group Elit has confirmed its interest in buying the Bulgarian state fork-lift producer Balkankar, a Balkankar senior official said.
